rv.q: Trap Door's excellent performers pace the stage before the play begins and we begin to feel what the life of a mannequin is like.
For all its absurdity, “The Mannequins’ Ball” shows us clearly and straightforwardly who the real dummies are.
It often feels like a bit of a reach for this large ensemble, with the exception of masterfully weird Marzena Bukowska, out of whose mouth the most abstract diatribes seem to make perfect sense.
Trap Door’s production of The Mannequin’s Ball is full of clever ideas, skilled performances, and a chaotic sensibility.
The Mannequin’s Ball takes audiences on a journey during the annual night of mannequin revelry where they can dance and move as freely as humans do.
